title: Cost and performance of large loads

videos.script: The shop is small, and every load has taken seconds. Real warehouses are not small. {{small}} First rule: measure before changing anything. {{measure}} Thirty thousand rows, three ways. One insert at a time, then in batches, then COPY. Sixty times apart. {{copy}} A larger table, made for the lesson. Three and a half million lines. {{big}} Finding one day: every row read, or straight there by an index. {{index}} Rebuilding all of it, or the last thirty days. Two seconds, or thirty milliseconds. {{window}} And reading a month, or six years. The cheapest page is the one never read.
